learning-kit use cases

Who uses learning-kit, what each of them can do, which front door offers each action, and the step-by-step flow of the main use cases.

The use cases at a glance

In short

There is one human actor, the learner. Every use case starts with them, either directly or through an agent acting for them. The 22 use cases fall into five groups: the topic loop, practice and recall, learning paths, the library and agents, and operations. Anything that needs judgement starts in Claude Code. The browser covers reading and quizzing. MCP agents can read everything, but they can only run no-stakes quizzes. S1S2

22use cases
1human actor
3external systems: grader, web, MCP client
5quiz modes

Actors

The system boundary is learning-kit as installed: the five skills, their subagents and the lk core. Subagents are inside the boundary because the skills spawn and control them. They aren't independent actors. S3

Primary and secondary actors

Use case diagram

Which front door offers which use case

The same data is reachable from three places, but each one is allowed to do different things. The rule: actions that need judgement, or that change a topic's stage or a path's plan, start in Claude Code. The only exception is the gate round, which the web app can start after a confirm. S5S2

Topic loop use cases

A topic moves through fixed stages. Each use case below is one stage, or a branch off it. lk refuses a move whose guard isn't met, so the order can't be skipped by accident. S8

UC-01 Start or resume a topic

Goal · trigger

Pick up a topic wherever it is. Trigger: /learn <topic> [--new] [--extend] [--depth aware|use|deep].

Postcondition

The topic exists, and the stage that comes next is either done or waiting on the learner with a clear instruction.
  1. Resolve the slug

    The skill matches the name to an existing topic (lk topic list --json). If there is none, it creates one with lk topic new.

  2. Size check

    If the name is a whole field ("system design") and not a path node, the skill asks once: build a path (UC-14), narrow the topic, or do an aware overview.

  3. Path context

    lk path for-topic gives the node's goal, focus, outcomes and prereqs. These steer research and the quiz.

  4. Dispatch on stage

    lk topic status → run that stage → lk topic advance → carry on in the same turn until a stage needs the learner (read, quiz, lab, note).

Exceptions: --new on an existing topic resumes it. --extend works only from scheduled. S3

UC-02 Capture prior knowledge

Before any teaching, the learner says what they already believe, plus 3 questions and 1 prediction (for --new: only the questions and the prediction). The skill writes their words verbatim to prior.md and corrects nothing. Guard to move on: prior.md exists and has at least 20 characters. S3S8

UC-03 Research a topic

  1. Plan facets

    2–5 facets come from the prior questions and the depth (a path node starts from its focus). The skill reuses sources first (lk source search).

  2. Collect in parallel

    One collect subagent per facet saves pages with lk source fetch. If a page can't be fetched: WebFetch, then lk source add --file.

  3. Aggregate

    An aggregate subagent writes research.md (every claim cites [S####], with visual blocks for processes) and a draft concept list.

  4. Merge and check

    lk concepts merge adds new concepts as new. lk read --check must report no broken visual blocks.

Guard to move on (read): research.md is at least 200 characters, at least one target concept exists, and there are no visual-block errors. S8

UC-04 Read the research

lk read <slug> renders research.md into research.html (diagrams, step cards, source chips, reading time) and opens it. The learner asks questions in chat. Each one and its short answer are appended to qa.md, and later become quiz material. The same page is served at /read/<slug> in the web app. S3

UC-05 Generate the quiz

  1. Author

    A quiz_author subagent drafts items for the target concepts. Its inputs include the prior beliefs and recent mistakes, which make good distractors. About half the items are free recall, and every core concept gets at least one.

  2. Validate

    lk quiz validate checks the schema per type, that sources are cited, and that an explanation is present.

  3. Fresh review

    A separate quiz_review subagent sees only the draft and the snapshots. It writes a corrected file.

  4. Import

    lk quiz import --reviewed-by opus assigns ids q0001…, the round and the version.

Guard to move on (quiz): every target concept has ≥ 2 fresh items (1 at aware), and every core concept has ≥ 1 fresh explain/predict item. S9

UC-06 Take a gate round

Preconditions

Stage is quiz. Coverage has no issues. Fewer than 3 gate rounds today, or an open gate session exists (it is resumed).

Postconditions

Attempts and mistakes are logged. Concepts are marked mastered or learning. The stage moves to note, lab, scheduled or reteach.
  1. Open

    /quiz or /learn runs lk serve --topic in the background, or the learner presses "Gate round" in the web app. The session takes fresh items for each target concept, easy to hard, with concepts interleaved.

  2. Answer

    Each answer has a confidence rating (guessing / unsure / sure) or "I don't know", and is saved on every Next. A reload resumes the quiz.

  3. Grade

    mcq/multi/order/cloze are graded by script. explain/predict go to the grader in batches of 8.

  4. Gate

    Pass = overall ≥ 80% and every core concept has an explain/predict answer ≥ 70%. Concepts that pass on their own are mastered even when the round fails.

  5. Report

    The results page shows per-concept bars, each answer against the expected one, and the next step. Closing the session ends lk serve, and the skill reports in at most 6 lines.

Exceptions: grader failure → grade_failed (UC-22). Daily cap reached → refused with "sleep on it". Not enough fresh items → refused with the coverage issues. S10S11

UC-07 Relearn missed concepts

After a failed gate (or when recall lapses a concept on a scheduled topic), the stage is reteach and round goes up by 1. A reteach subagent writes reteach/round-N.md aimed only at what was missed. The learner reads it, then UC-05 runs again for the remaining targets with fresh items. A relearn that passes goes straight back to scheduled. S8S12

UC-08 Run a lab (deep topics)

At depth deep, a passed gate leads to lab. The skill designs one small experiment, and the learner writes their prediction before running it. lab/RESULTS.md records prediction vs actual. Guard to move on: lab/RESULTS.md exists. S8

UC-09 Write and review the own-words note

  1. Capture

    /note saves the note typed, dictated, or from the editor. Only dictation slips are fixed, and earlier notes are kept as note.vN.md.

  2. Review

    A fresh note_review subagent scores 5 criteria from 0 to 2: correctness, coverage, own_words, when_not, connections. It checks hardest on the gate's weak concepts.

  3. Record

    lk note record computes the result. Pass = total ≥ 8, correctness = 2, and no criterion at 0. On a pass the stage moves to scheduled and recall cards are created.

Alternative: a failed correctness check leads to a relearn (concepts set to learning, then reteach). Any other failure means revising the note. S13

UC-10 Extend a finished topic

/learn <topic> --extend calls lk topic extend: version + 1, round + 1, stage back to research. New concepts come in as new with added_in = version, so the next gate covers only the new material. Mastered concepts stay in recall. S8

Practice and recall use cases

UC-11 Practice quiz

A no-stakes round: up to n items (10 by default) picked at random from the topic's whole bank, spent items included. It can start from /quiz --practice, the web app's "Practice" button, or MCP start_quiz. It writes attempts (mode practice) and the mistakes log, but doesn't change the stage or the recall schedule. Practice attempts don't count as spent gate items. S7S14

UC-12 Spaced recall session

  1. Due queue

    Cards due today or earlier, ordered by due date and then lowest retrievability, capped at 30 a day. Up to 3 not-yet-due confident mistakes (last seen ≥ 3 days ago) are added. The list is shuffled, then interleaved round-robin across topics.

  2. Reword /recall only

    A reword subagent writes variants that keep each card's origin and concept. Variants that fail validation are dropped, and the original item is used instead.

  3. Answer and reschedule

    Each result becomes an FSRS grade (score < 0.5 → Again, < 0.8 → Hard, otherwise Hard/Good/Easy depending on confidence) and updates the origin card.

  4. Lapse

    An Again marks the concept lapsed. The topic page and lk path next then send the learner to relearn (UC-07).

Exception: nothing due → refused with the next due date. S15S16

UC-13 Review the mistakes log

Every answer scoring below 0.5 in any mode except placement is appended to mistakes.jsonl and mistakes.md, with the learner's answer, the expected one and the reason. A confidence of "sure" marks it ⚠ confident. The web app lists them at #/mistakes, MCP through mistakes. S14

Learning path use cases

UC-14 Plan a learning path

  1. Intake needs the learner

    One AskUserQuestion call (purpose, level, hours per week, deadline) and one open question → intake.md.

  2. Curriculum research

    2–3 collect subagents save syllabi, books' tables of contents and roadmaps into the source bank.

  3. Plan, then review

    A path_plan subagent writes plan.md and a draft. A fresh path_review subagent corrects it. lk path validate must pass.

  4. Approve and import needs the learner

    The learner sees a compact table and asks for changes once. Then lk path import stores version 1.

Rules checked by the import: prereqs point only to earlier nodes; ≤ 15 nodes; a capstone has ≥ 2 prereqs; the first node is full; intake.md and plan.md exist. A re-plan needs --reason. Removing a node whose topic has started needs --force. S17

UC-15 Placement quiz and per-node decisions

A short quiz (≤ 3 items per node, ≤ 24 in total) finds steps the learner already knows. The result is stored only in path.placement: no attempts, no mistakes, no topics created. Per node, test_out needs mean ≥ 0.8 and mean confidence ≥ 2.5. fast_track needs mean ≥ 0.5. Anything lower is learn. These are recommendations only. The learner decides, and lk path override … tested_out refuses without evidence at the bar unless --force is given. S18

UC-16 Walk the path

/path <slug> asks lk path next for exactly one action and carries it out. Actions are checked in this order: plan → placement → review (a node finished since the last plan review) → relearn (a finished node has lapsed concepts) → checkpoint → resume → expand / learn → complete. Any session gets the same answer, so the path resumes correctly from anywhere. S19

UC-17 Milestone checkpoint

When every node of a milestone is satisfied, at least 2 of them have actually been learned, and no checkpoint has been taken yet, a mixed quiz is due. It draws up to 3 items from each learned node (free recall first), interleaved across topics. Its answers update the existing recall cards, and an Again lapses the concept. The result is stored in path.checkpoints[<milestone>] with its weak topics. S19S14

Library, agent and operations use cases

UC-18 Browse the library

lk web serves the library at 127.0.0.1:8765. It has five views: #/ (recall due, unfinished sessions, paths, topics, recent sessions), #/path/<slug>, #/topic/<slug> (stage, docs, concepts, quiz coverage as counts, session history), #/session/<id> (quiz or results), and #/mistakes. Docs open as reader pages. The quiz bank is shown only as counts, so browsing can't spoil fresh gate items. S6S20

UC-19 Quiz in chat through MCP

The agent calls start_quiz (practice or recall), then repeats next_question → asks the learner → answer_question with the learner's words verbatim and their own confidence, and ends with finish_quiz. The server instructions forbid answering for the learner, giving hints, or revealing correctness before the finish. Gate, placement and checkpoint are refused with a message naming the skill to use. S2

UC-20 Browse data through MCP

Read-only tools (overview, get_path, get_topic, read_doc, list_sessions, session_results, recall_due, mistakes, search_sources, read_source) plus four lk:// resources. Source text comes back labelled untrusted. S2

UC-21 Install and configure

python lk.py install --home <dir> writes ~/.learning-kit.json, creates topics/ paths/ sources/ sessions/, a starter config.json and a README, and renders the 5 skills into ~/.claude/skills. It must be re-run after editing a skill or moving the repo. S21

UC-22 Recover from failed grading

If claude -p is missing, times out or returns bad JSON, the session becomes grade_failed. The answers and the script-graded results are kept. The learner presses "Retry grading" or runs lk grade <id>. As a last resort, lk grade <id> --pending prints what still needs grading, the agent grades it by hand, and lk grade <id> --apply file.json finishes the session. S11S22
